html:
The Tawahka are an Indigenous people of the middle Patuca River in eastern Honduras, in the forests of the Mosquitia. They speak a form of the Mayangna (Sumu) language, one of the Misumalpan family.

They live in a few villages by the river, farming, fishing and hunting, and travel by dugout canoe. Their numbers are small, about a thousand or two. In 1999 Honduras created the Tawahka Asangni Biosphere Reserve on their land. Neighbours: Miskito and Pech.
